children: Index provider FTSE Russell said it was monitoring developments after Turkey's Capital Markets Board ordered the liquidation of several investment funds, according to a statement sent to Reuters.

Turkey on Thursday ordered the liquidation of 131 investment funds worth $18.3 billion, managed by seven portfolio companies, and appointed Is Yatirim and state-run lender Ziraat to oversee the process.
FTSE Russell said it would provide an update on all equity markets in its annual country classification review on October 6.

The index provider also referred to an August statement in which it flagged difficulties reconciling official free-float figures with its methodology and postponed some index changes involving Turkish-listed securities.
